input.quote: Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
input.rationale: Section 3.4 gives Customer a convenience right on one month's notice (better than the 60–90 day fallback) and IBM has no convenience right anywhere in the Agreement (§3.3 is mutual for-cause only; §3.2 is end-of-term non-renewal on 90 days) — both consistent with the preferred position. The material failure is the exit cost: §3.4(b) conditions the right on paying early termination charges "specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments" with no cap, and §3.5 contains no refund of prepaid Charges. That fails the fallback ceiling of an early-termination fee not exceeding three months' fees, so we cap the charges at three months' recurring Charges and add the pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges. We have left the one-month notice and Attachment A mechanic intact.

ops.oldText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
ops.newText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, provided that such charges will not exceed, in the aggregate, three (3) months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services. IBM will refund to Customer any prepaid Charges for the period after the effective date of termination.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We accept the early termination charge mechanic but need it capped at three months' recurring Charges and paired with a refund of prepaid Charges, consistent with our playbook position that convenience termination should not carry an open-ended penalty.
proposal.summary: Cap early termination charges at three months' recurring Charges and add pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges.
